P1.evidence: No setter. The four-part frame ran properly for only the second time in this batch: 'It's just an opportunity for me to understand where you are today. You know, where do you go and what's been holding you back? And if I can feel like we can genuinely help you, will recommend one of the many options that we have.' Where you are, where you are going, what is in the way and the options are all present. No agreement was sought afterwards, and the opener was the lead-source variant — 'What was it that you originally saw from Trevor that stood out enough to you to book this call?' — rather than the scripted help question.

P2.evidence: The only P2c hit anywhere in this batch, and it matters: 'Okay. High cholesterol. Is there anything else I need to be aware of? Any limitations in your body?' followed by 'How long have we been aware of this?' That is the right question, asked properly, and it produced type 2 diabetes and high cholesterol known for three years. The capability clearly exists in this rep's repertoire. What follows is the gap — nothing was asked about medication, treating physician, glucose management or clearance for loaded training, and the disclosure was never referenced again except to sell fasting. Work was covered fully including the desk-bound check. Height was never asked and current weight is only inferable from the 30-pound target. Training week, current results and diet were all skipped — on a diabetic. Sleep and energy score partial because both were discussed at length but volunteered rather than elicited.

P3.evidence: Comprehensive. The day-to-day question ran twice, and when the prospect answered about how he feels now rather than how he wants to feel, the rep caught it and redirected: 'Sorry to interrupt you there, Tony... How do you want to operate and feel in your body in the day to day?' The ripple was driven properly through personal impact, family, nieces and nephews, and the consulting business, and then to identity: 'who does that allow you to become?' produced confidence and 'it radiates', which the rep then probed twice — 'When you say it radiates, in what way?' and 'tell me more.' Best moment of the phase is at 00:21:59, where the prospect said something meaningful in passing and the rep refused to let it go: 'You said a very, very powerful sentence there. Sometimes people are dependent on you and you're not there... can you just give me maybe a recent example?' He asked twice. The prospect could not produce one, which is itself useful information.

P4.evidence: The root cause was reached and named — 'would you say procrastination has been the main thing that has kept you stuck for the past 10 to 15 years?' — 'Definitely.' But P4e is only partial because the rep supplied the answer rather than eliciting it: 'Would you say that the root of the procrastination comes from a place of being comfortable?' is a leading question and the prospect simply agreed, then added better material of his own that went unexplored — 'most people are not health oriented, it all depends on your circle... if you have a circle, people kind of hold you accountable, most people don't have that.' That is the accountability gap named unprompted and it was not built on. Past attempts were barely covered; a kinesiology degree and a history of personal training were mentioned in the first minute and never examined.

P5.evidence: The first properly run consequence frame in this batch, and it should be the coaching exemplar. 'What happens if you don't?' produced 'if I don't get it together, the quality of life will probably be very, very bad in the coming years. That's to put it lightly.' The settle-for move followed immediately and in its scripted form: 'But is that something you're willing to accept? A lot of people I speak to, especially in America, are okay with that.' — 'Yeah, no, not at all.' The line in the sand ran twice, as 'are you actually ready to take that step? Just man-to-man here?' and earlier as 'is it ultimately time to change that?', and the urgency question ran cleanly: 'Why now as opposed to in November?' Only the explicit 'why not' is missing. Note that this is the one call in the batch where phase 5 ran and the prospect still declined — because his objection was scope, not conviction.

P6.evidence: Correctly sequenced and unambiguous. When the prospect asked about price at 00:36:19, the rep deferred it properly — 'I'll cover that in a moment, but alignment is super important for us' — and ran the scale, getting 'I think 100% this is going to be very good', then followed up with 'What gives you the confidence to say that?'. P6a ran as 'do you feel internally capable of following Trevor's step-by-step process, being a good student?' and got a considered yes about structure removing the procrastination problem. A clear yes existed before the offer. The all-in question was still never asked, and here it would have been decisive: it is the question designed to surface 'I don't need this much', which is exactly what killed the deal four minutes later.

P11.evidence: No programme was sold, so phase 11 applies only to the ancillary product. Payment was collected and confirmed on the recording — 'All right. Payment successful. We emailed you a receipt' — which earns a partial rather than a hit because it is a $199 subscription rather than a programme. The Trevor onboarding call does not attach to Primal University, so P11b is not applicable. P11c is a miss: a recurring monthly charge was set up with no agreement, no contract and nothing signed. P11d is partial and was handled patiently — the rep walked him through Skool account creation, troubleshot a missing email prompt and a locked card, and confirmed access before ending.

objection_plays.detail: Price was raised — 'that's a bit pricey' — so the trigger is present, but the rep read it correctly as not being a capacity problem and did not run the play, which was the right judgement. The prospect said plainly 'I'm definitely not saying it's not worth the money' and confirmed he would simply have used a credit card. Two OC-adjacent moves ran: the worth-it question ('do you believe that's actually worth the investment?') and the payment-mechanics question. No isolation, no financial picture, no payment plan — correctly, since none of them addresses an objection about scope. The one genuinely OC move that did run backfired: 'if you had the capability to figure out on your own, you would have for the past 10 to 15 years' drew an immediate and accurate correction, 'not really the capability, it's just the motivation.'
No request for time; he made a decision on the call and acted on it.
No third-party approval gate. He has no partner or children involved in the decision.
Timing was pre-empted by the rep's 'Why now as opposed to in November?' during phase 5 and never became an objection.
Fear was explored as discovery material via the skydiving frame, and the prospect engaged with it comfortably, but it never surfaced as a blocker to the purchase.

The reduced-scope objection, and this is the fourth prospect in three days to raise it after Roy Norman, Soneel Raj and Atul Sharma. Tony stated it more clearly than anyone: 'I don't really need that intensive. I was looking at something structured to do, maybe, okay, this day do this, this day do that.' He also asked directly about a cheaper product he had seen Trevor advertise — 'he was advertising the kettlebell routine in a PDF. What do you offer in that?' — and that question was never answered. There is no scripted play, and the rep improvised the right one by conceding fit and offering Primal University, which closed. Four occurrences in three days is not a rep problem; it is a missing rung in the product ladder that Primal University is quietly filling without being part of the published offer.

Clinical-fit gap, in its metabolic rather than musculoskeletal form. A prospect with diagnosed type 2 diabetes and high cholesterol requires, at minimum, a question about medication and current medical management before any nutrition or fasting guidance is offered. The playbook has no such requirement, no stop condition, and no language for deferring pending clinical input — so the rep sold fasting protocols instead. The gap is more dangerous here than in the musculoskeletal cases because the pathway to harm is same-day rather than gradual.

notes: The best-run call in this batch on process: a genuine four-part frame, the only proper health-conditions question anywhere in these twelve files, an excellent phase 3, the first real consequence frame, and a clean phase 6 in the right order. It still lost the programme, because the objection was never about conviction or money — it was that a man with a kinesiology degree wanted structure, not supervision, and said so five different ways. Two things follow. For the rep: the all-in question would have surfaced that before the price and is the one check he has never run in six calls. For the business: he asked the right clinical question, got type 2 diabetes as the answer, and the process gave him nowhere to take it, so he sold fasting to a diabetic. That is a playbook defect, not a coaching one, and it is the most urgent single fix in this batch.
